caption_enhancement.scope_note: No blanket rule was added for all captions. Captions are eligible only when they explicitly identify the item-specific reporting function.

must_have: The article title explicitly identifies the study as randomized, using randomized/randomised or an unambiguous equivalent.
The article title explicitly identifies the study as randomized/randomised or as a randomized/randomised trial.
not_if: The sentence is not the title or only says clinical trial without random allocation language.
The abstract or methods describe randomization but the title does not.
Randomization is mentioned only in the abstract or body rather than the title.
1a.definition: Identification as a randomised trial in the title

must_have: The first substantive abstract sentence is used as the corpus marker for a structured abstract that reports trial design, methods, results, and conclusions.
The first sentence or structured abstract text indicates a structured summary covering trial design, methods, results, and conclusions.
not_if: The sentence is a title, author line, keyword list, or abstract section header alone.
The sentence contains only background/objective content without abstract structure.
Do not label an abstract section header itself; label the first substantive abstract sentence under the corpus convention.
1b.definition: Structured summary of trial design, methods, results, and conclusions

must_have: Explains the scientific context and the evidence gap or clinical uncertainty that justified conducting this trial.
Explains scientific background, clinical problem, prior evidence, evidence gap, or rationale for why the trial was undertaken.
not_if: The sentence only states the study objective/hypothesis; use 2b.
The sentence reports trial results or interpretation rather than pre-trial rationale.
Do not annotate more than the few best rationale sentences when the background spans many sentences.
The sentence states the specific objective/hypothesis without explaining why the trial was needed; use 2b.
A literature fact without a link to the trial rationale is insufficient unless it helps explain why the study was needed.
2a.definition: Scientific background and explanation of rationale

must_have: States the trial-specific question in terms of an objective, aim, purpose, or hypothesis, ideally identifying the intervention/comparison and target outcome or population.
States the specific objective, aim, purpose, research question, or hypothesis of the trial.
not_if: The sentence only gives broad disease background or rationale; use 2a.
The sentence defines outcome measures without an explicit objective/hypothesis; consider 6a.
The sentence only gives prior evidence or disease background without this trial objective; use 2a.
A future or external trial objective is not the objective of the current report.

must_have: Names the trial design and, when reported, the allocation ratio; design descriptors can include parallel, factorial, crossover, cluster, superiority, non-inferiority, or equivalence.
Describes the trial design type and/or allocation ratio, such as parallel, factorial, crossover, multicenter, superiority/noninferiority, blinded/placebo-controlled design.
not_if: The sentence only describes interventions without design structure; use 5.
The sentence only describes random sequence generation or concealment; use 8a/8b/9/10.
The sentence only states eligibility, intervention dose, or outcome definition without describing trial design.
The sentence says participants were randomized to receive a treatment dose/comparator; that is usually intervention details (5), not trial design (3a).
The sentence reports results or conclusions, even if it contains the word randomized.
A sentence that only says participants were randomized to receive named interventions is usually intervention assignment (5) unless it also characterizes the overall design.
3a.definition: Description of trial design (such as parallel, factorial) including allocation ratio

must_have: Reports an important change to the planned methods after trial commencement and gives the reason for the change.
Describes important changes to trial methods after commencement, with a reason.
not_if: The sentence describes planned methods from the original protocol without a later change.
The sentence reports why the trial ended/stopped; use 14b.
The sentence describes planned design at trial start rather than a change after commencement.
A protocol detail or amendment without indicating a post-commencement change and reason is insufficient.
3b.definition: Important changes to methods after trial commencement (such as eligibility criteria), with reasons

must_have: States inclusion and/or exclusion criteria that determine who was eligible to participate in the current trial.
States eligibility, inclusion, or exclusion criteria for participants.
not_if: The sentence only states setting/location; use 4b.
The sentence only describes baseline characteristics of enrolled participants; use 15.
The sentence describes study location/setting rather than who was eligible; use 4b.
Do not label broad population summaries or registry-subgroup descriptions as eligibility criteria unless inclusion/exclusion criteria are explicit.
A population description alone is not an eligibility criterion unless it expresses a selection requirement.

must_have: Identifies the setting and geographic or institutional locations where participants were recruited or data were collected.
States settings, locations, sites, clinics, hospitals, countries, centers, or time/place where data were collected.
not_if: The sentence only gives participant eligibility criteria; use 4a.
The sentence only gives recruitment/follow-up dates; use 14a.
The sentence describes eligibility criteria rather than study setting/location; use 4a.
Do not label equipment, scanners, coils, assays, or measurement platforms as settings/locations when they define outcome assessment; consider 6a.
Equipment manufacturers, imaging platforms, laboratories, or analytic facilities are not study settings unless they identify participant/data-collection locations.
4b.definition: Settings and locations where the data were collected

must_have: Describes what each group actually received with enough operational detail for replication, such as content, dose, route, frequency, timing, duration, and permitted adaptations.
Describes what each group received with enough intervention/comparator details for replication, including dose, timing, delivery, duration, or administration rules.
not_if: The sentence describes outcome assessment or measurement procedure rather than treatment; use 6a.
The sentence only describes design/allocation ratio; use 3a.
A procedure performed solely to measure an outcome is 6a, not an intervention, even if it involves infusion, imaging, sampling, or equipment.
5.definition: The interventions for each group with sufficient details to allow replication, including how and when they were actually administered

must_have: Completely defines each prespecified primary and secondary outcome, including the outcome variable, metric or instrument, aggregation method, and assessment time point when available.
Defines pre-specified primary or secondary outcome measures/endpoints, including what was assessed and, when available, how and when assessed.
Measurement apparatus, imaging protocols, laboratory assays, marker definitions, timing of assessment, and quantification procedures can satisfy 6a when they define how outcomes were assessed.
not_if: The sentence describes the statistical comparison method; use 12a.
The sentence reports outcome results; use 17a/17b.
The sentence describes additional/exploratory measures rather than primary/secondary outcomes unless they are explicitly trial outcomes.
The sentence describes a future or external trial rather than outcome measures in the current trial.
A measurement detail is not sufficient when it is unrelated to a prespecified trial outcome; require outcome linkage from the sentence or paragraph context.
6a.definition: Completely defined pre-specified primary and secondary outcome measures, including how and when they were assessed

must_have: Reports a change to a trial outcome after commencement and explains why it changed.
Describes changes to trial outcomes/endpoints after trial commencement, with reasons.
not_if: The sentence describes original outcomes only; use 6a.
The sentence describes other method changes; use 3b.
A change to statistical analysis, intervention, eligibility, or sample size is not 6b unless the outcome itself changed.
6b.definition: Any changes to trial outcomes after the trial commenced, with reasons

must_have: Explains how the target sample size was calculated, normally including the assumed effect, variability/event rate, alpha, power, allocation, and allowance for attrition when reported.
Explains how sample size was determined, including assumptions such as effect size, power, alpha, dropout, or target enrollment.
not_if: The sentence only reports actual enrollment/randomized numbers; use 13a.
The sentence only describes statistical analysis methods; use 12a.
A final enrollment count without calculation assumptions is participant flow, not sample-size determination.

must_have: Describes planned interim analyses and/or stopping rules, including timing, statistical boundaries, decision criteria, or responsible independent monitoring when reported.
Explains interim analyses, stopping guidelines, stopping boundaries, or monitoring rules when applicable.
not_if: The sentence reports actual trial stop/end reason; use 14b.
The sentence describes final statistical analysis without interim/stopping plan; use 12a.
An ordinary repeated analysis at several follow-up times is not an interim analysis unless linked to early stopping or monitoring.
7b.definition: When applicable, explanation of any interim analyses and stopping guidelines

must_have: States the method or algorithm used to generate the random allocation sequence.
Describes the method used to generate the random allocation sequence.
not_if: The sentence only describes blocking/stratification/restriction; use 8b.
The sentence describes allocation concealment mechanism; use 9.
The sentence says who generated/enrolled/assigned; use 10.
The sentence only describes blocking/stratification/restriction without how the sequence was generated; use 8b.
Stratification, blocking, allocation ratio, or concealment mechanism alone does not identify sequence generation.
8a.definition: Method used to generate the random allocation sequence

must_have: States the type of randomization and details of restrictions such as stratification, blocking, minimization, and block size.
Describes type of randomization and restrictions such as blocking, block size, stratification, minimization, or allocation ratio.
not_if: The sentence only says the sequence was computer-generated; use 8a.
The sentence describes concealment or implementation roles; use 9/10.
The sentence only says computer-generated/random list without restriction details; use 8a.
A computer-generated sequence alone is 8a unless restriction details are also present.
8b.definition: Type of randomisation; details of any restriction (such as blocking and block size)

must_have: Describes the mechanism that concealed the allocation sequence until assignment, including safeguards against foreknowledge or manipulation.
Describes the allocation concealment mechanism and steps that hid the sequence until assignment.
not_if: The sentence only says who generated/enrolled/assigned participants; use 10.
The sentence only describes sequence generation; use 8a/8b.
The sentence identifies who generated/enrolled/assigned without concealment mechanism; use 10.
Who generated, enrolled, or assigned participants is implementation (10), not concealment mechanism.
9.definition: Mechanism used to implement the random allocation sequence, describing any steps taken to conceal the sequence until interventions were assigned

must_have: Identifies who generated the sequence, who enrolled participants, and/or who assigned interventions.
States who generated the allocation sequence, who enrolled participants, and/or who assigned participants to interventions.
not_if: The sentence only describes concealment mechanism without human/role implementation details; use 9.
The sentence only describes sequence generation method; use 8a.
The sentence only describes concealment mechanism such as sealed envelopes or central concealment; use 9.
A concealment device or central system without an actor/role is 9 rather than 10.
10.definition: Who generated the random allocation sequence, who enrolled participants, and who assigned participants to interventions

must_have: Identifies which trial parties were blinded after assignment and how blinding was maintained or implemented.
States who was blinded/masked after assignment and/or how blinding was maintained.
not_if: The sentence only says interventions looked similar; use 11b.
The sentence describes allocation concealment before assignment; use 9.
The sentence only says placebo/intervention looked similar; use 11b.

Blinded event adjudication or blinded image analysis is not necessarily full CONSORT blinding of participants, care providers, or outcome assessors unless the blinded role and post-assignment context are explicit.
Blinded laboratory reading or event adjudication alone is not automatically 11a unless those assessors are the relevant outcome assessors and the sentence describes blinding to treatment assignment.
11a.definition: If done, who was blinded after assignment to interventions and how

must_have: Describes how intervention and comparator were made similar in appearance, taste, smell, administration, or other relevant characteristics.
Describes similarity of interventions/comparators relevant to blinding, such as matching placebo appearance, taste, color, packaging, or content.
not_if: The sentence only states who was blinded; use 11a.
The sentence describes the active intervention dose or schedule without similarity/blinding; use 5.
The sentence only names who was blinded; use 11a.
Calling the study double-blind or using a placebo without similarity details is insufficient for 11b.
11b.definition: If relevant, description of the similarity of interventions

must_have: Describes the statistical analysis for each primary and secondary outcome, including comparison model, analysis population, covariates when part of the main model, handling of missing data, multiplicity, and inferential conventions when reported.
Describes statistical methods used to compare groups for primary or secondary outcomes.
Statistical software, significance thresholds, transformations, normality checks, multiplicity corrections, and confidence-limit reporting can all be valid statistical-method evidence.
not_if: The sentence defines outcomes/endpoints without statistical method; use 6a.
The sentence describes methods for subgroup/adjusted/additional analyses specifically; use 12b.
The sentence reports results of analyses; use 17a/18.
Reporting a confidence interval or p-value as a result is not a method unless the sentence specifies the analysis/reporting convention.
12a.definition: Statistical methods used to compare groups for primary and secondary outcomes

must_have: Describes methods specifically used for additional analyses, including subgroup, adjusted, sensitivity, per-protocol, interaction, or exploratory analyses.
Describes statistical methods for additional, subgroup, adjusted, sensitivity, exploratory, or ancillary analyses.
not_if: The sentence describes the main statistical method for primary/secondary outcomes; use 12a.
The sentence reports results of additional analyses; use 18.
A covariate-adjusted model that is the prespecified main analysis may remain 12a; determine whether the analysis is main or additional from context.
12b.definition: Methods for additional analyses, such as subgroup analyses and adjusted analyses

must_have: Reports, for each randomized group, numbers assigned, receiving intended intervention, and analyzed for the primary outcome; a flow diagram or caption may supply this evidence.
Reports participant flow counts by group: randomly assigned, received intended treatment, and/or analyzed for the primary outcome.

A substantive table/figure caption or title can satisfy 13a when it explicitly identifies participant flow, trial profile, CONSORT flow, or subject disposition; the caption need not contain every count if it clearly names the flow evidence shown in the associated figure/table.
not_if: The sentence reports losses/exclusions and reasons after randomization; use 13b.
The sentence reports baseline characteristics; use 15.
The sentence reports denominators for each analysis population; use 16 if focused on analysis denominator.
The sentence focuses on losses/exclusions and reasons after randomization; use 13b.
Baseline clinical characteristics are 15 even when the paragraph begins with randomized counts; use table/paragraph function to resolve ambiguous counts.
Do not label a bare token such as “Figure 1”, “Table 2”, or a generic “Study design” heading as 13a unless the caption itself identifies participant flow/disposition.
A caption focused on reasons for withdrawal, discontinuation, exclusion, or loss belongs to 13b rather than 13a.
negative_cues: study design caption without flow content
13a.definition: For each group, the numbers of participants who were randomly assigned, received intended treatment, and were analysed for the primary outcome

must_have: Reports losses and exclusions after randomization for each group together with reasons.
Reports losses and exclusions after randomization with reasons.
Short standalone sentences giving the reason for discontinuation, withdrawal, loss, exclusion, or protocol deviation are valid 13b evidence.
A table/figure caption can support 13b when it explicitly identifies withdrawals, discontinuations, exclusions, losses to follow-up, or reasons for these post-randomization losses.
not_if: The sentence only reports flow counts without reasons; use 13a.
The sentence reports harms as trial outcomes rather than reasons for discontinuation; use 19.
The sentence reports adverse event rates as harms rather than participant-flow reasons; use 19.
Adverse events are 19 when reported as safety outcomes; use 13b when adverse events function as reasons for withdrawal, discontinuation, or exclusion.
Do not infer 13b from a generic participant-flow caption unless the caption itself identifies losses/exclusions or their reasons.
An adverse-event caption reporting safety outcomes by group is 19, not 13b, unless its primary function is discontinuation/withdrawal due to adverse events.
negative_cues: adverse event table without withdrawal function
13b.definition: For each group, losses and exclusions after randomisation, together with reasons

must_have: Provides calendar dates or date ranges for recruitment and the duration or dates of follow-up.
States dates or periods of recruitment and/or follow-up.
not_if: The sentence only states setting/location without dates; use 4b.
The sentence explains why the trial stopped; use 14b.
The sentence explains why the trial stopped or ended early; use 14b.
Assessment time points alone are outcome timing (6a), not recruitment/follow-up dates, unless they define the trial follow-up period.
14a.definition: Dates defining the periods of recruitment and follow-up

must_have: Explains why the trial ended or was stopped, particularly when termination was earlier than planned.
Explains why the trial ended or was stopped, including early termination or external stopping reason.
not_if: The sentence only gives planned recruitment/follow-up dates; use 14a.
The sentence describes interim stopping guidelines rather than actual ending reason; use 7b.
The sentence only gives recruitment/follow-up dates without explaining trial stopping; use 14a.
Normal completion at the planned endpoint without a reason for stopping is not 14b.
14b.definition: Why the trial ended or was stopped

must_have: Reports baseline demographic and clinical characteristics separately by randomized group, including a valid baseline table or caption.
Reports or points to baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group.
Table or figure headings such as “Table 1 Baseline Characteristics” are valid evidence when they identify baseline characteristic reporting.
A terse standalone table/figure title is valid 15 evidence when it directly names baseline demographic or clinical characteristics, even if it contains no numerical values in the title itself.
not_if: The sentence only reports randomization/flow counts; use 13a.
The sentence reports post-treatment outcome results; use 17a/18.
A pretreatment value used only as part of an outcome change calculation is not necessarily baseline-characteristics reporting.
Do not reject “Table 1 Baseline Characteristics” as a bare heading: under the corpus convention it is a checklist-bearing caption/title.
Do not use 15 for captions titled “change from baseline”; those usually report post-treatment outcomes and belong to 17a or 18.
15.definition: A table showing baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group

must_have: Gives the denominator included in each analysis and states whether participants were analyzed in their originally assigned groups.
Reports the number of participants included in each analysis and/or whether analyses followed original assigned groups such as intention-to-treat.

A table/figure caption can support 16 when it explicitly identifies the analysis population, analysis set, denominator, intention-to-treat population, per-protocol population, or participants included in an analysis.
not_if: The sentence only reports randomized/received/analyzed flow counts; use 13a.
The sentence describes statistical method without denominator/analysis population; use 12a.
The sentence reports participant flow counts without analysis denominator or analysis population; use 13a.
General participant flow counts without identifying the analysis denominator or analysis set are 13a.

Do not assign 16 merely because an outcome-table title contains the phrase “intention-to-treat”; the caption must primarily identify the analysis population or denominator rather than only the outcome result.
16.definition: For each group, number of participants included in each analysis and whether the analysis was by original assigned groups

must_have: For each primary and secondary outcome, reports results for each group and an estimated effect with precision when applicable; valid evidence may span linked sentences or a table/figure caption under corpus annotation conventions.
Reports results for primary or secondary outcomes by group and/or effect estimates with precision.

A standalone table/figure title or caption is valid 17a evidence when it directly identifies results for a prespecified primary or secondary outcome, such as a named outcome, endpoint, efficacy measure, change from baseline, or survival analysis.
Verified caption-style examples include “Figure 1 Changes in Carotid Wall Area” and “Table 3 Change From Baseline in MRI Measures” when those measures are treated as main trial outcomes.
not_if: The sentence reports additional/subgroup/adjusted/exploratory analysis results; use 18.
The sentence reports harms; use 19.
The sentence interprets results in Discussion rather than reporting Results-section estimates; use 22.
For binary outcomes with both absolute and relative effects, consider 17b.
The sentence is in Discussion/Abstract and only summarizes or interprets results without original Results-section estimates.
The sentence reports a p-value or qualitative significance without an effect estimate or precision when the annotation requires full outcome reporting.
The sentence reports exploratory/biomarker/subgroup/additional analyses rather than primary/secondary outcome results; consider 18.

Do not require a confidence interval in every individual sentence if the gold convention accepts linked result sentences or table/figure headings; require clear outcome-result function and use paragraph context.

Do not reject a substantive outcome caption solely because it lacks a numerical estimate in the caption text; the corpus may annotate the caption as the evidence pointer to the associated table/figure.

Do not label legend-only sentences, symbol definitions, axis explanations, abbreviation keys, or display-format notes as 17a; for example, “Bars = means with 95% confidence intervals” does not itself report an outcome result.
Do not use 17a for a caption naming ancillary biomarkers, exploratory measures, subgroup analyses, pharmacokinetic analyses, correlations, or other non-main analyses; use 18.
positive_cues: Figure 1 Changes in Carotid Wall Area
Table 3 Change From Baseline in MRI Measures
negative_cues: blood measures for biomarkers when ancillary
17a.definition: For each primary and secondary outcome, results for each group, and the estimated effect size and its precision

must_have: For a binary outcome, reports both absolute and relative effect measures; absolute group event rates plus a relative estimate may jointly satisfy the item.
For a binary outcome, presents both absolute and relative effect sizes or enough paired absolute and relative reporting.

A table/figure caption can support 17b only when it explicitly identifies a binary outcome presentation that includes or points to both absolute and relative effect reporting; a generic response-rate caption alone is insufficient.
not_if: The outcome is continuous or ordinal without binary event/proportion interpretation.
The sentence gives only a percentage/proportion or only a risk ratio/odds ratio; use 17a.
Harms binary outcomes usually belong to 19 unless clearly primary/secondary outcome reporting.
A response rate comparison without a relative effect measure should not automatically be accepted as 17b under the official definition, even if corpus annotations occasionally differ.

Do not promote an outcome caption to 17b merely because it contains percentages, response rates, event rates, or the word binary; require evidence of both absolute and relative effects in the caption or tightly linked table/figure context.
17b.definition: For binary outcomes, presentation of both absolute and relative effect sizes is recommended

must_have: Reports results of analyses beyond the main primary/secondary outcome analyses and identifies whether they were prespecified or exploratory when the report provides that distinction.

Reports results of other analyses, including subgroup, adjusted, ancillary, exploratory, post hoc, sensitivity, or additional analyses, while distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory when stated.
Treat biomarker, correlation, subgroup, adjusted, exploratory, ancillary, lipid/inflammation marker result sentences as 18 when they are not clearly the main primary/secondary outcome results.

A standalone table/figure title or caption is valid 18 evidence when it directly identifies ancillary, exploratory, subgroup, adjusted, biomarker, laboratory-marker, correlation, pharmacokinetic, gene-expression, or other non-main analyses.

Verified caption-style examples include “Table 4 Blood Measures for Lipids, Diabetes Control, and Markers of Inflammation” and “Figure 2 Changes in Lipids and C-Reactive Protein” when these are annotated as additional analyses.
not_if: The sentence reports main primary/secondary outcome results; use 17a.
The sentence describes methods for additional analyses; use 12b.
The sentence interprets additional findings in Discussion; use 22.
A biomarker is not automatically item 18; it is 17a when prespecified as a primary/secondary outcome and 18 when ancillary, exploratory, subgroup, adjusted, or otherwise additional.
Do not require the words “exploratory” or “subgroup” in the caption when article context clearly establishes the named measures as additional analyses.
Do not assign 18 solely because a caption names a biomarker; use outcome hierarchy and article context, because a biomarker can be a prespecified primary/secondary outcome and therefore 17a.
positive_cues: Table 4 Blood Measures for Lipids, Diabetes Control, and Markers of Inflammation
Figure 2 Changes in Lipids and C-Reactive Protein
18.definition: Results of any other analyses performed, including subgroup analyses and adjusted analyses, distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory

must_have: Reports important harms or unintended effects for each group, including event counts/rates, severity, seriousness, withdrawals due to harms when functioning as safety evidence, and absence of important harms when explicitly reported.
Reports important harms, adverse events, unintended effects, safety outcomes, or adverse event counts/rates by group.

A direct adverse-event, serious-adverse-event, safety, toxicity, death, or harms table/figure caption can satisfy 19 when it identifies safety outcomes or unintended effects, including captions for zero-event findings.
not_if: The sentence explains participant losses/exclusions due to adverse events; use 13b if the function is participant flow.
The sentence interprets safety in Discussion; consider 22.
The sentence defines safety monitoring outcome in Methods; use 6a.
A reason for attrition should be 13b when its reporting function is participant flow rather than safety comparison.
Do not label a caption as 19 merely because adverse events are mentioned as reasons for withdrawal or discontinuation; that reporting function is 13b.
Do not label generic safety-monitoring methods or adjudication procedures as 19; item 19 requires reported harms results.
negative_cues: withdrew due to adverse event as flow reason
19.definition: All important harms or unintended effects in each group

must_have: Names a concrete limitation and links it to possible bias, imprecision, limited power, multiplicity, measurement constraints, follow-up, or interpretive uncertainty.
Reports a specific trial limitation, potential bias, imprecision, multiplicity issue, limited power, missing measure, or design/data constraint.
Specific inability to evaluate safety, dose adequacy, plaque features, selection, measurement, follow-up, or sample-size limitations should be treated as 20.
not_if: The sentence merely says the study has limitations without naming one.
The sentence gives interpretation or implications without a concrete limitation; use 22.
The sentence is about generalizability/applicability; use 21.
A recommendation for future research is not itself a limitation unless it is tied to a stated constraint of the present trial.
20.definition: Trial limitations, addressing sources of potential bias, imprecision, and multiplicity of analyses

must_have: Assesses whether and how the findings apply beyond the enrolled participants and trial setting, considering population, intervention delivery, setting, outcomes, and follow-up.
Discusses generalizability, external validity, or applicability of trial findings to other populations, settings, patients, or practice contexts.
not_if: The sentence only interprets clinical meaning without applicability/external-validity framing; use 22.
The sentence only names a limitation; use 20.
Merely naming the target population or saying findings are important does not establish generalizability.

must_have: Interprets the results in light of study hypotheses, potential benefits and harms, limitations, multiplicity, and relevant external evidence without overstating the findings.
Interprets trial findings consistently with results, balances benefits and harms, compares with other evidence, or states clinical/scientific implications.
not_if: The sentence only reports raw Results-section estimates; use 17a/18/19.
The sentence only states a specific limitation; use 20.
The sentence only addresses external validity/generalizability; use 21.
Summary-box statements should usually not be annotated unless the item appears nowhere else.
A raw result repeated in Discussion without interpretive, comparative, or implication language may be unannotated under corpus conventions rather than automatically 22.
22.definition: Interpretation consistent with results, balancing benefits and harms, and considering other relevant evidence

must_have: Provides both the trial registry name and registration number.
States the registration number and name of the trial registry.
not_if: The sentence only says the study was approved by an ethics committee or gives protocol access; use 24 for protocol access.
The sentence cites a registry without registration number when no registry identification is given.
A registry name without a registration identifier, or an identifier without clear trial-registration context, may be incomplete.
23.definition: Registration number and name of trial registry

must_have: States where the full trial protocol can be accessed, such as a supplement, journal appendix, repository, or web location.
States where the full trial protocol can be accessed.
not_if: The sentence only gives trial registration number/name; use 23.
The sentence only describes protocol approval/amendment without access location.
Saying the study followed a protocol or citing a prior methods paper does not necessarily identify access to the full protocol.
24.definition: Where the full trial protocol can be accessed, if available

must_have: Identifies sources of funding or material support and describes the role of funders or sponsors in design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, writing, and publication decisions.
States sources of funding/support, supply of drugs/materials, sponsor support, and/or role of funders.
not_if: The sentence only reports conflicts of interest, authorship contribution, ethics approval, or acknowledgements without funding/support or funder role.
The sentence only describes registration/protocol access; use 23/24.
Conflict-of-interest, authorship, or manuscript drafting statements alone are not funding-role evidence unless linked to the funder or sponsor.
25.definition: Sources of funding and other support, role of funders

17a__18.rule: Use 17a for prespecified primary/secondary outcome results; use 18 for additional analyses. Outcome status, not biomarker vocabulary or statistical significance, is decisive.
17a__18.choose_first_when: The analysis reports a prespecified primary or secondary endpoint, including its planned subgroup-free main comparison.
17a__18.choose_second_when: The analysis is subgroup, adjusted beyond the main model, sensitivity, interaction, exploratory, ancillary, post hoc, correlation, or otherwise additional.
17a__18.do_not: Do not automatically treat biomarkers/lipids as 18 or any analyzed result as 17a; determine whether the measure was a prespecified primary/secondary outcome.

examples.sentence: (A) In both left and right carotid arteries, canakinumab retarded progression of wall area compared with placebo.

global_rules: If a sentence does not fit neatly into any CONSORT item, do not annotate it.
If automatic sentence splitting divides one relevant sentence into multiple fragments, annotate all relevant fragments with the applicable item.
Do not annotate subsection titles alone; prefer sentences with actual checklist content.
Use the typical CONSORT section as a strong prior, but allow cross-section annotation when the item appears only outside its usual section.
Other information items 23, 24, and 25 may be annotated in any section when explicitly stated.
In abstracts, annotate 1b when appropriate; additionally annotate items mentioned only in the abstract, such as trial registration.
For table or figure evidence, annotate the caption when available; otherwise annotate the narrative sentence that refers to the table or figure.
Avoid annotating caption sentences that only explain symbols, abbreviations, or formatting and do not report checklist content.
Summary boxes such as “What this study adds” should usually not be annotated unless they contain an item not addressed elsewhere.
For anaphoric interpretation, annotate the sentence that carries the checklist meaning; do not over-annotate antecedent sentences solely to resolve pronouns.
For outcome-related items, first decide whether the sentence concerns primary/secondary outcomes or additional analyses; this boundary affects 6a/6b, 12a/12b, 17a/17b, and 18.
For 17a vs 17b, determine whether the outcome is binary and whether both absolute and relative effect sizes are presented.
For item 20, annotate only specific limitations; do not annotate generic statements that merely say the study has limitations.
When a sentence explicitly satisfies multiple item definitions, preserve multiple labels rather than forcing a single label prematurely.
Pass 2 gold data confirms strong section priors: Methods for items 3–12, Results for items 13–19, Discussion for items 20–22, and flexible sections for administrative items 23–25.

Gold examples include table and figure captions as valid evidence when captions directly identify baseline characteristics, participant disposition, efficacy outcomes, blood measures, or adverse events.
Do not annotate bare section headers such as “Patients”, “Methods”, or “Study design” unless the text itself contains checklist-relevant content.

When the training examples annotate table titles such as baseline characteristics, subject disposition, or efficacy outcomes, treat the caption/title as evidence for the corresponding item rather than discarding it as too short.

Use outcome hierarchy explicitly: define outcomes in 6a/6b, analyze primary/secondary outcomes in 12a, analyze additional/subgroup/adjusted outcomes in 12b, report primary/secondary results in 17a/17b, and report other analyses in 18.
Treat FP_ANNOTATION_UNDERLABEL and FP_VALID_ALTERNATIVE as soft evidence of possible annotation incompleteness, not as hard negative rules.
For Results items, prefer Results-section evidence over Discussion/Abstract restatements unless the target item is only available outside the typical section.
For 17a, do not accept qualitative result summaries without sufficient estimate/precision when a stricter annotated Results sentence is available.
For 6a, measurement instruments, laboratory assays, imaging protocols, and quantification procedures are valid outcome-assessment evidence when tied to trial outcomes.
Standalone table and figure headings can be valid evidence when they name baseline characteristics, outcome results, additional analyses, harms, or participant flow.
Interpret each prototype as a reporting-function rule, not a keyword classifier: identify what role the sentence plays in reporting the current trial.
Apply official CONSORT conceptual scope first, then the corpus annotation convention for sentence selection, section use, captions, and allowable context.

For compound CONSORT requirements, evidence may be distributed across linked sentences, captions, tables, or paragraph context; do not require every component to appear in one isolated sentence unless the corpus does so.
Do not transfer evidence from a future, external, prior, or cited trial to the current trial merely because it contains a CONSORT-like phrase.

When official guidance and corpus annotations appear inconsistent, preserve the corpus convention for extraction scoring but mark the pattern as a potential annotation alternative rather than turning it into a universal negative rule.
Outcome status is decisive for 6a/12a/12b/17a/17b/18: first establish whether the measure is primary, secondary, or additional, then classify definition, method, or result.
Use the function of adverse-event language to distinguish participant-flow reasons (13b), harms reporting (19), and benefit-harm interpretation (22).

Caption-specific extraction rule: first decide whether the text is a substantive caption/title or only a display fragment. Substantive captions that identify checklist content are eligible evidence; bare figure/table numbers, symbol keys, abbreviation lists, axis labels, and formatting notes are not.

For terse standalone captions, classify by the reporting function named in the caption: participant flow/disposition → 13a or 13b; baseline characteristics → 15; analysis population → 16; main primary/secondary outcome → 17a/17b; ancillary/exploratory/subgroup/biomarker analysis → 18; harms/safety results → 19.

A caption may be valid even without numerical values because it points to the associated table/figure content under the corpus annotation convention; however, the caption must identify the relevant reporting function rather than merely say “Table”, “Figure”, or “Results”.
Do not use caption vocabulary alone to resolve 17a versus 18. Determine whether the named measure is a prespecified primary/secondary outcome or an additional analysis from article context.

When a multi-sentence caption contains both substantive result text and legend/formatting text, annotate only the sentence(s) carrying checklist content and exclude sentences that only define symbols, bars, abbreviations, units, or graphical layout.
